parts.reasoning: The object is a carrot. We approximate it as an elongated conical body with low mass. Carrots are mostly water and fibrous tissue, giving them a density close to water (approx. 1000 kg/m^3). Assuming an average-sized carrot with a volume around 60-80 cubic centimeters, the mass would be around 0.07 kg. The surface is slightly rough and organic, resulting in moderate static and dynamic friction coefficients. Restitution is low because it is a relatively soft, non-bouncy organic material. For collision modeling, a convex decomposition or convex hull provides a good approximation of the tapering root, while the leafy stems can either be ignored or modeled with lightweight, simplified geometry depending on simulation requirements. Contact offsets should be small due to the size of the object.
